solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Primate of Nigeria's first objective is revolutionary

indicators.note: a revolution turns something right round, so the letters run backwards
the first of a word is its opening letter, so only that letter is kept

parts.note: opening letter of the country's name
an objective is an aim
taken as written

explanation.surface: A question about what a leading Nigerian churchman is really trying to achieve, and whether it is radical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primate' looks like an archbishop in this surface, but it means an ape; N, AIM and IS read backwards give SIMIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Simian is a noun for an ape or monkey, the zoological order that includes humans and apes.

clue.text: Horseman stripped knight captured by perverse henchman

indicators.note: stripping takes off the outer covering, so both end letters go
something captured is held inside its captor, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: sick humour is twisted or perverse
a rider, with its first and last letters removed
K is a standard abbreviation for knight

explanation.surface: A rider unseated and stripped of rank, taken prisoner by a villain's twisted underling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horseman' tempts as the definition, but it is stripped wordplay; the henchman at the end is what is defined.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidekick is an assistant or close follower, as a henchman is to a villain.

clue.text: Crooked young lady starts to harangue acclaimed writer

parts.note: a miss is a young unmarried woman

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters, so only those are kept

parts.note: opening letters of both words
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: A dishonest young woman begins berating a celebrated author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crooked' suggests a dishonest person in the surface but is the definition, meaning bent out of shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Something misshapen is deformed or twisted out of its proper form, which is one sense of crooked.

clue.text: Open uprising in Canberra jail

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means reading from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards
the letters sit inside the run of words that follows, spanning a word break

parts.note: found across the end of the city and the start of the prison word

explanation.surface: A public revolt breaks out in an Australian prison.
explanation.walkthrough: RAJA is concealed in 'CanberRA JAil'; read upwards it gives AJAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A door that is ajar is slightly open, so the adjective matches the definition directly.

clue.text: Accompanied by physician, Earl and wife retired

parts.note: to be accompanied by someone is to be with them
DR is the abbreviation for doctor
E is the abbreviation for earl
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: An aristocrat and his wife, with their doctor in tow, went off to bed or into retirement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' seems to describe the couple stepping down, but it is the definition: went away.
explanation.definitionFit: To retire from a room or company is to withdraw, so the past tenses are synonyms.

clue.text: Extremely idiotic diver lying about shipping hazard

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two end letters, so only those are kept

parts.note: first and last letters of the word

indicators.note: turned about means facing the other way, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a grebe is a diving water bird

explanation.surface: A very foolish scuba diver loafs about in waters where vessels are at risk.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'diver' is not a person but the grebe, a water bird that dives for food.
explanation.definitionFit: Icebergs are floating masses of ice that sink vessels, the classic danger to ships at sea.

clue.text: Unconventional uni has time for the arts

indicators.note: unconventional means not in the usual order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: An unorthodox university makes room in its timetable for arts subjects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Has' looks like a verb in the surface but is part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The humanities are the academic fields of literature, history and philosophy, collectively called the arts.

clue.text: Priest taken in by Catholic artefact

indicators.note: to be taken in is to be admitted inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: RC is short for Roman Catholic
Eli is the priest who raised Samuel in the Bible

explanation.surface: A cleric is fooled by a religious object of the Catholic church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken in' reads as 'deceived', but it means placed inside; Eli is the crossword's usual priest.
explanation.definitionFit: A relic is an object surviving from an earlier time, such as a saint's remains or an old artefact.

clue.text: Hardy country women regularly feast on it

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for women

indicators.note: at regular intervals means every other letter is kept

parts.note: second and fourth letters of the word
'it' is an old euphemism for sex appeal or sex

explanation.surface: Robust rural women often gorge themselves on something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hardy' looks like an adjective for tough country women; it is Thomas Hardy, the English novelist, and 'on' places the last piece after the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Hardy set his novels in Wessex, his fictional version of south-west England named after the old Saxon kingdom.

clue.text: Part of coast RAF effectively hit with heavy fire

indicators.note: only a portion of the following words is used, so the letters are concealed inside them

parts.note: runs across the end of the first word, the whole second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Along a stretch of coastline the air force effectively bombards the enemy.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is concealed in 'coaST RAF Effectively'; the RAF really did do this to coastal targets.
explanation.definitionFit: To strafe is to attack ground targets with machine-gun fire from low-flying aircraft.

clue.text: Pick apart detective's cover

parts.note: DI is a detective inspector, plus the possessive S
a mantle is a cloak or covering layer

explanation.surface: Someone tries to unpick an investigator's disguise.
explanation.walkthrough: DI is the British police rank Detective Inspector; the possessive S stays in.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismantle a thing is to take it to pieces, which is to pick it apart.

clue.text: Discovered charm ultimately softens stubborn types

indicators.note: dis-covered means with its cover taken off, so the outer letters go

parts.note: an amulet is a charm; drop its end letters

indicators.note: what comes ultimately comes last, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Charm, once found out, eventually wins over the obstinate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discovered' reads as 'found out', but it means uncovered: AMULET loses its outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Mules are proverbially obstinate animals, so obstinate people are called mules.

clue.text: Declaration of old king's long-serving chancellor

indicators.note: a declaration is something spoken out, so it is the sound that counts

parts.note: Old King Cole is the merry old soul of the nursery rhyme

explanation.surface: A proclamation from a former monarch's longest-serving minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old king' is Old King Cole of the nursery rhyme, whose name sounds like the German chancellor's.
explanation.definitionFit: Helmut Kohl led Germany as Chancellor for sixteen years, from 1982 to 1998.

clue.text: Berate clan about bread and wine store

indicators.note: moved about means turned around and rearranged, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: Someone tells off a family over the state of their bakery and off-licence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bread and wine store' sounds like a shop, but it means the church receptacle for the Eucharist.
explanation.definitionFit: In Catholic churches the tabernacle is the locked box holding consecrated communion hosts.

clue.text: Kitchen appliance cheapskate initially rejected is under fifty-one pounds

indicators.note: the initial part is turned away, so the opening letter is dropped
in a down entry, being under means coming after, so one piece follows the others

parts.note: L is fifty and I is one in Roman numerals
quid is British slang for a pound sterling, singular or plural
a miser, losing its first letter

explanation.surface: A gadget for the kitchen is turned down by a skinflint because it costs under fifty-one pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: Quid is British slang for a pound; the miser, minus M, sits at the bottom of the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A liquidiser is the British name for a blender, a machine that purees food in the kitchen.

clue.text: Overturn measure relating to head coverings

parts.note: a cap is a head covering; used attributively, as a hat size is named
a size is a measure; the size relating to caps

explanation.surface: A proposal to repeal a law about hats.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay reads backwards: the measure relating to head coverings is a cap size, with the plural dropped as in 'shoe size'.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat that capsizes overturns in the water, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Threaten to go out, say, after golf

indicators.note: one thing coming after another sets them side by side in that order

parts.note: Golf is the NATO alphabet word for G
to utter is to say

explanation.surface: Someone warns they will head out, perhaps after a round of golf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like 'for example' but is a verb here, meaning speak.
explanation.definitionFit: A candle flame gutters when it flickers and nearly dies, on the point of being extinguished.

clue.text: Free love sired sinners

indicators.note: letters set free can fall into any order, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: Children of free love turn out to be wrongdoers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free love' is a single phrase in the surface; split it, and the first word is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Evildoers are people who do wrong, and sinners likewise commit moral wrongs.

clue.text: Prevented growth obstructing the judge's heart

indicators.note: something obstructing a passage sits in the middle of it, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: taken as written
a wart is a small growth on the skin

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the central letter of the five-letter word

explanation.surface: A growth blocked the judge's heart, stopping it working.
explanation.walkthrough: The growth goes inside THE after its second letter, then the middle of 'judge' follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To thwart a plan is to prevent it succeeding, so thwarted and prevented are synonyms.

clue.text: A French star essentially struggled to produce instrumental?

parts.note: un is French for 'a'
the sun is a star

indicators.note: the essence of something is at its core, so only the central letter is kept

parts.note: the central letter of the nine-letter word

explanation.surface: A French celebrity battled to make a record without vocals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Instrumental' tempts as 'helpful', but with the question mark it means music without singing.
explanation.definitionFit: An instrumental piece has no vocals, so in a playful sense nothing in it is sung.

clue.text: Epicurean rogue drunkenly embracing male model

indicators.note: to embrace is to wrap one's arms round, so one piece holds another
a drunk staggers about unsteadily, so the letters lurch into a new order

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging
M is the abbreviation for male
the Model T was Ford's famous early car

explanation.surface: A pleasure-seeking scoundrel, drunk, has his arms round a male model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' gives T, from the Ford Model T; 'Epicurean' is a noun here, a lover of fine food.
explanation.definitionFit: An epicure is a connoisseur of fine food and drink, which is exactly what a gourmet is.

clue.text: Spot bishop from Flanders forsaking female

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: to forsake is to abandon, so a letter is left out

parts.note: Flemish means coming from Flanders
F is the abbreviation for female; this is the letter removed

explanation.surface: Look out for a Belgian bishop who has abandoned a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spot' reads as the verb 'notice', but it is the noun, a mark; Flanders is the Dutch-speaking north of Belgium.
explanation.definitionFit: A blemish is a small mark or flaw on a surface, such as a spot on the skin.

clue.text: Supporting bum in arrears

definitions.meaning: first meaning: backing someone, as in standing with them
second meaning: the buttocks, British slang
third meaning: late with payments owed

explanation.surface: A layabout who backs others yet never pays what he owes.
explanation.walkthrough: Three separate meanings of one word; 'bum' here is the British word for backside, not a tramp.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means backing someone, the backside, and late with payments, so it covers all three senses.

clue.text: Pay no heed to Italian gentleman disowning son

indicators.note: to disown is to cast off, so a letter is thrown out

parts.note: signore is the Italian for sir or gentleman
S is the abbreviation for son; this is the letter removed

explanation.surface: An Italian patriarch rejects his son and pays him no attention.
explanation.walkthrough: SIGNORE loses its S to leave the answer; the surface family drama fits the definition neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: To ignore someone is to disregard them, which is paying no attention or heed to them.

clue.text: Drug Andy distributed outside church in Luxembourg, say

indicators.note: being outside something means wrapping round it, so one piece holds another
things distributed are spread around, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A man called Andy hands out narcotics outside a church in Luxembourg.
explanation.walkthrough: Luxembourg seems to be where the scene happens, but with 'say' it is an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Luxembourg is the world's only remaining grand duchy, a state ruled by a grand duke.

clue.text: Seaman thanks upstanding European moderate

parts.note: AB is an able seaman

indicators.note: standing up in a down entry means reading from the bottom upwards

parts.note: ta is British informal for thanks
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A sailor thanks an honest, moderate European.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moderate' looks like an adjective describing the European, but it is the verb; ta is British slang for thank you.
explanation.definitionFit: To abate is to lessen in intensity, which is what it means to moderate something.

clue.text: Concept middleman oddly ignored

indicators.note: ignoring the odd-numbered positions leaves only the even ones

parts.note: second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: The notion that a go-between was strangely overlooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' seems to mean 'strangely', but it points at the odd-numbered letters to drop.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea is a thought or notion formed in the mind, the same as a concept.

clue.text: Reject physio's conclusion supporting surgeon

indicators.note: in a down entry, a support sits underneath, so it comes after

parts.note: a vet is an animal surgeon

indicators.note: the conclusion of a word is its end, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A doctor turns down the physiotherapist's diagnosis, though it backs up the surgeon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Surgeon' here is a veterinary surgeon, the formal British title for a vet.
explanation.definitionFit: To veto a proposal is to reject it formally, using a right to block it.

clue.text: Stones hit about pursuing love

indicators.note: one that pursues another comes behind it, so it follows

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

indicators.note: turned about means facing the other way, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: to slap is to hit

explanation.surface: Rocks are thrown around by someone chasing romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love' is zero, the tennis score, written as the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Opals are iridescent gemstones, and gems are commonly called stones.

clue.text: Caught in pit, Steerpike mostly lived on dried fruits?

indicators.note: something inside goes within the other piece
most but not all means the last letter is lost

parts.note: a mine is a pit dug for coal or ore
the setter refers to themself by pseudonym
lived on, as in subsisted on food
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: The setter, trapped down a pit, survived mostly on raisins and currants.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often name themselves for ME; the question mark flags that the definition describes rather than defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Mincemeat is the sweet mix of raisins, currants and suet used in British mince pies.

clue.text: Detest value placed on administrator

indicators.note: in an across entry, putting one thing onto another adds it to the end

parts.note: short for executive
to rate is to value

explanation.surface: An executive resents having a price put on his work.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue lists the second piece first; 'on' puts the value after the administrator.
explanation.definitionFit: To execrate is to loathe or curse, a stronger and more formal synonym of detest.

clue.text: Sat around island in state of readiness

indicators.note: to go around something is to enclose it, so one piece holds another

parts.note: a model posed, or sat, for a portrait
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: Someone waited on an island, ready for action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sat' is a model sitting for an artist, not merely sitting down.
explanation.definitionFit: To be poised is to be balanced and prepared, ready to act at any moment.
